ambient: Encompassing on all sides; circumfused; investing. "Ambient air." Milton. "Ambient clouds." Pope. | Something that surrounds or invests; as, air . . . being a perpetual ambient. Sir H. Wotton.
amazon: 1. One of a fabulous race of female warriors in Scythia; hence, a female warrior. 2. A tall, strong, masculine woman; a virago. 3. (Zoöl.) A name numerous species of South American parrots of the genus Chrysotis Amazon ant (Zoöl.), a species of ant (Polyergus rufescens), of Europe and America.
amplectant: Clasping a support; as, amplectant tendrils. Gray.
among: 1. Mixed or mingled; surrounded by. They heard, And from his presence hid themselves among The thickest trees. Milton. 2. Conjoined, or associated with, or making part of the number of; in the number or class of. Blessed art thou among women. Luke i. 28. 3. Expressing a relation of dispersion, distribution, etc.; also, a relation of reciprocal action.
amateurship: The quality or character of an amateur.
amphichroic: Exhibiting or producing two colors, as substances which in the color test may change red litmus to blue and blue litmus to red.
amphibious: 1. Having the ability to live both on land and in water, as frogs, crocodiles, beavers, and some plants. 2. Pertaining to, adapted for, or connected with, both land and water. The amphibious character of the Greeks was already determined: they were to be lords of land and sea. Hare. 3. Of a mixed nature; partaking of two natures.
americanism: 1. Attachment to the United States. 2. A custom peculiar to the United States or to America; an American characteristic or idea. 3. A word or phrase peculiar to the United States.
amenability: The quality of being amenable; amenableness. Coleridge.
amharic: Of or pertaining to Amhara, a division of Abyssinia; as, the Amharic language is closely allied to the Ethiopic. -- n. The Amharic language (now the chief language of Abyssinia).
amplitude: 1. State of being ample; extent of surface or space; largeness of dimensions; size. The cathedral of Lincoln . . . is a magnificent structure, proportionable to the amplitude of the diocese. Fuller. 2. Largeness, in a figurative sense; breadth; abundance; fullness. (a) Of extent of capacity or intellectual powers. "Amplitude of mind." Milton.
amazonian: 1. Pertaining to or resembling an Amazon; of masculine manners; warlike. Shak. 2. Of or pertaining to the river Amazon in South America, or to its valley.
amnesty: 1. Forgetfulness; cessation of remembrance of wrong; oblivion. 2. An act of the sovereign power granting oblivion, or a general pardon, for a past offense, as to subjects concerned in an insurrection.
amboynawood: A beautiful mottled and curled wood, used in cabinetwork. It is obtained from the Pterocarpus Indicus of Amboyna, Borneo, etc.
amidogen: A compound radical, NH2, not yet obtained in a separate state, which may be regarded as ammonia from the molecule of which one of its hydrogen atoms has been removed; -- called also the amido group, and in composition represented by the form amido.
amoebiform: Resembling an amoeba; amoeba-shaped; changing in shape like an amoeba. Amoeboid movement, movement produced, as in the amoeba, by successive processes of prolongation and retraction.
ambitus: 1. The exterior edge or border of a thing, as the border of a leaf, or the outline of a bivalve shell. 2. (Rom. Antiq.) A canvassing for votes.
ampliate: To enlarge. To maintain and ampliate the external possessions of your empire. Udall. | Having the outer edge prominent; said of the wings of insects.
ambulation: The act of walking. Sir T. Browne.
ambrosial: 1. Consisting of, or partaking of the nature of, ambrosia; delighting the taste or smell; delicious. "Ambrosial food." "Ambrosial fragrance." Milton. 2. Divinely excellent or beautiful. "Shakes his ambrosial curls." Pope.
amphibian: Of or pertaining to the Amphibia; as, amphibian reptiles.
amylogen: That part of the starch granule or granulose which is soluble in water.
ambrosian: Of or pertaining to St. Ambrose; as, the Ambrosian office, or ritual, a formula of worship in the church of Milan, instituted by St. Ambrose. Ambrosian chant, the mode of signing or chanting introduced by St. Ambrose in the 4th century.
amyl: A hydrocarbon radical, C5H11, of the paraffine series found in amyl alcohol or fusel oil, etc.
amir: 1. Emir. (old) 2. One of the Mohammedan nobility of Afghanistan and Scinde.
amido: Containing, or derived from, amidogen. Amido acid, an acid in which a portion of the nonacid hydrogen has been replaced by the amido group. The amido acids are both basic and acid. -- Amido group, amidogen, NH2.
amplificatory: Serving to amplify or enlarge; amplificative. Morell.
ambition: 1. The act of going about to solicit or obtain an office, or any other object of desire; canvassing. (old) [I] used no ambition to commend my deeds. Milton. 2. An eager, and sometimes an inordinate,… | To seek after ambitiously or eagerly; to covet. Pausanias, ambitioning the sovereignty of Greece, bargains with Xerxes for his daughter in marriage. Trumbull.
ambitiousness: The quality of being ambitious; ambition; pretentiousness.
ambry: 1. In churches, a kind of closet, niche, cupboard, or locker for utensils, vestments, etc. 2. A store closet, as a pantry, cupboard, etc. 3. Almonry. [Improperly so used]
ambiguously: In an ambiguous manner; with doubtful meaning.
amphigory: A nonsense verse; a rigmarole, with apparent meaning, which on further attention proves to be meaningless. [Written also amphigouri.]
amazedness: The state of being amazed, or confounded with fear, surprise, or wonder. Bp. Hall.
ambush: 1. A disposition or arrangement of troops for attacking an enemy unexpectedly from a concealed station. Hence: Unseen peril; a device to entrap; a snare. Heaven, whose high walls fear no assault or… | 1. To station in ambush with a view to surprise an enemy. By ambushed men behind their temple Dryden. 2. To attack by ambush; to waylay.
ambassadorial: Of or pertaining to an ambassador. H. Walpole.
amatorial: Of or pertaining to a lover or to love making; amatory; as, amatorial verses.
amorosity: The quality of being amorous; lovingness. Galt.
amends: Compensation for a loss or injury; recompense; reparation. [Now const. with sing. verb.] "An honorable amends." Addison. Yet thus far fortune maketh us amends. Shak.
ametropia: Any abnormal condition of the refracting powers of the eye. -- Am`e*trop"ic, a.
amphistomous: Having a sucker at each extremity, as certain entozoa, by means of which they adhere.
amphiscians: The inhabitants of the tropic, whose shadows in one part of the year are cast to the north, and in the other to the south, according as the sun is south or north of their zenith.
ambassadorship: The state, office, or functions of an ambassador.
amazing: Causing amazement; very wonderful; as, amazing grace. -- A*maz"ing*ly, adv.
ammunition: 1. Military stores, or provisions of all kinds for attack or defense. (old) 2. Articles used in charging firearms and ordnance of all kinds; as powder, balls, shot, shells, percussion caps, rockets, etc. 3. Any stock of missiles, literal or figurative. Ammunition bread, shoes, etc., such as are contracted for by government, and supplied to the soldiers. [Eng.]
amontillado: A dry kind of cherry, of a light color. Simmonds.
amel: To enamel. (old) Enlightened all with stars, And richly ameled. Chapman.
amia: A genus of fresh-water ganoid fishes, exclusively confined to North America; called bowfin in Lake Champlain, dogfish in Lake Erie, and mudfish in South Carolina, etc. See Bowfin.
amblyopic: Of or pertaining to amblyopy. Quain.
amoebaeum: A poem in which persons are represented at speaking alternately; as the third and seventh eclogues of Virgil.
amomum: A genus of aromatic plants. It includes species which bear cardamoms, and grains of paradise.
amid: In the midst or middle of; surrounded or encompassed by; among. "This fair tree amidst the garden." "Unseen amid the throng." "Amidst thick clouds." Milton. "Amidst acclamations." "Amidst the splendor and festivity of a court." Macaulay. But rather famish them amid their plenty. Shak. Syn. -- Amidst, Among.
ambi: A prefix meaning about, around; -- used in words derived from the Latin.
amalgam: 1. An alloy of mercury with another metal or metals; as, an amalgam of tin, bismuth, etc. Note: Medalists apply the term to soft alloys generally. 2. A mixture or compound of different things. 3. | To amalgamate. Boyle. B. Jonson.
amphitheatrical: Of, pertaining to, exhibited in, or resembling, an amphitheater.
amygdalin: A glucoside extracted from bitter almonds as a white, crystalline substance.
amenable: 1. (Old Law) Easy to be led; governable, as a woman by her husband. (old) Jacob. 2. Liable to be brought to account or punishment; answerable; responsible; accountable; as, amenable to law. Nor is man too diminutive . . . to be amenable to the divine government. I. Taylor. 3. Liable to punishment, a charge, a claim, etc. 4. Willing to yield or submit; responsive; tractable.
amylaceous: Pertaining to starch; of the nature of starch; starchy.
amphioxus: A fishlike creature (Amphioxus lanceolatus), two or three inches long, found in temperature seas; -- also called the lancelet. Its body is pointed at both ends. It is the lowest and most generalized of the vertebrates, having neither brain, skull, vertebræ, nor red blood. It forms the type of the group Acrania, Leptocardia, etc.
ammonal: An explosive consisting of a mixture of powdered aluminium and nitrate of ammonium.
ambassy: See Embassy, the usual spelling. Helps.
amitosis: Cell division in which there is first a simple cleavage of the nucleus without change in its structure (such as the formation of chromosomes), followed by the division of the cytoplasm; direct cell division; -- opposed to mitosis.
amused: 1. Diverted. 2. Expressing amusement; as, an amused look.
amnion: A thin membrane surrounding the embryos of mammals, birds, and reptiles.
amish: Of, pertaining to, or designating, the followers of Jacob Amman, a strict Mennonite of the 17th century, who even proscribed the use of buttons and shaving as "worldly conformity". There are several branches of Amish Mennonites in the United States.
amidships: In the middle of a ship, with regard to her length, and sometimes also her breadth. Totten.
amniotic: Of or pertaining to the amnion; characterized by an amnion; as, the amniotic fluid; the amniotic sac. Amniotic acid. (Chem.) See Allantoin.
amine: One of a class of strongly basic substances derived from ammonia by replacement of one or more hydrogen atoms by a basic atom or radical.
amovability: Liability to be removed or dismissed from office. T. Jefferson.
ambigenous: Of two kinds. (Bot.) Partaking of two natures, as the perianth of some endogenous plants, where the outer surface is calycine, and the inner petaloid.
amusive: Having power to amuse or entertain the mind; fitted to excite mirth. -- A*mu"sive*ly, adv. -- A*mu"sive*ness, n.
amoroso: In a soft, tender, amatory style.
amulet: An ornament, gem, or scroll, or a package containing a relic, etc., worn as a charm or preservative against evils or mischief, such as diseases and witchcraft, and generally inscribed with mystic forms or characters. Note: [Also used figuratively.]
ametabola: A group of insects which do not undergo any metamorphosis. [Written also Ametabolia.]
amorphism: A state of being amorphous; esp. a state of being without crystallization even in the minutest particles, as in glass, opal, etc. Note: There are stony substances which, when fused, may cool as glass or as stone; the glass state is spoken of as a state of amorphism.
ammoniac: Of or pertaining to ammonia, or possessing its properties; as, an ammoniac salt; ammoniacal gas. Ammoniacal engine, an engine in which the vapor of ammonia is used as the motive force. | The concrete juice (gum resin) of an umbelliferous plant, the Dorema ammoniacum. It is brought chiefly from Persia in the form of yellowish tears, which occur singly, or are aggregated into masses.
ambages: A circuit; a winding. Hence: Circuitous way or proceeding; quibble; circumlocution; indirect mode of speech. After many ambages, perspicuously define what this melancholy is. Burton.
amniota: That group of vertebrates which develops in its embryonic life the envelope called the amnion. It comprises the reptiles, the birds, and the mammals.
amaze: 1. To bewilder; to stupefy; to bring into a maze. (old) A labyrinth to amaze his foes. Shak. 2. To confound, as by fear, wonder, extreme surprise; to overwhelm with wonder; to astound; | To be astounded. (old) B. Taylor.
amphigamous: Having a structure entirely cellular, and no distinct sexual organs; -- a term applied by De Candolle to the lowest order of plants.
amole: Any detergent plant, or the part of it used as a detergent, as the roots of Agave Americana, Chlorogalum pomeridianum, etc. [Sp. Amer. & Mex.]
ammodyte: (a) One of a genus of fishes; the sand eel. (b) A kind of viper in southern Europe. (old)
amorpha: A genus of leguminous shrubs, having long clusters of purple flowers; false or bastard indigo. Longfellow.
amateurish: In the style of an amateur; superficial or defective like the work of an amateur. -- Am`a*teur"ish*ly, adv. -- Am`a*teur"ish*ness, n.
amicable: Friendly; proceeding from, or exhibiting, friendliness; after the manner of friends; peaceable; as, an amicable disposition, or arrangement. That which was most remarkable in this contest was . . . the amicable manner in which it was managed. Prideoux.
amazonite: A variety of feldspar, having a verdigris-green color.
amiableness: The quality of being amiable; amiability.
amphoric: Produced by, or indicating, a cavity in the lungs, not filled, and giving a sound like that produced by blowing into an empty decanter; as, amphoric respiration or resonance.
ammiral: An obsolete form of admiral. "The mast of some great ammiral." Milton.
ambrosin: An early coin struck by the dukes of Milan, and bearing the figure of St. Ambrose on horseback.
amalgamate: 1. To compound or mix, as quicksilver, with another metal; to unite, combine, or alloy with mercury. 2. To mix, so as to make a uniform compound; to unite or combine; as, to amalgamate two races; | 1. To unite in an amalgam; to blend with another metal, as quicksilver. 2. To coalesce, as a result of growth; to combine into a uniform whole; to blend; as, two organs or parts amalgamate.
ameliorative: Tending to ameliorate; producing amelioration or improvement; as, ameliorative remedies, efforts.
ament: A species of inflorescence; a catkin. The globular ament of a buttonwood. Coues.
amioid: Like or pertaining to the Amioidei. -- n. One of the Amioidei.
amrita: Immorality; also, the nectar conferring immortality. -- a. Ambrosial; immortal.
amoret: 1. An amorous girl or woman; a wanton. (old) J. Warton. 2. A love knot, love token, or love song. (pl.) Love glances or love tricks. (old) 3. A petty love affair or amour. (old)
amnesia: Forgetfulness; also, a defect of speech, from cerebral disease, in which the patient substitutes wrong words or names in the place of those he wishes to employ. Quian.
amenorrhoea: Retention or suppression of the menstrual discharge.
amphibological: Of doubtful meaning; ambiguous. "Amphibological expressions." Jer. Taylor. -- Am*phib`o*log"ic*al*ly, adv.
amylene: One of a group of metameric hydrocarbons, C5H10, of the ethylene series. The colorless, volatile, mobile liquid commonly called amylene is a mixture of different members of the group.
amylose: One of the starch group (C6H10O5)n of the carbohydrates; as, starch, arabin, dextrin, cellulose, etc.
amerce: 1. To punish by a pecuniary penalty, the amount of which is not fixed by law, but left to the discretion of the court; as, the amerced the criminal in the sum on the hundred dollars. Note: The penalty of fine may be expressed without a preposition, or it may be introduced by in, with, or of. 2. To punish, in general; to mulct.
americanplan: In hotels, aplan upon which guests pay for both room and board by the day, week, or other convenient period; -- contrasted with European plan.
amigo: A friend; -- a Spanish term applied in the Philippine Islands to friendly natives.
amphi: A prefix in words of Greek origin, signifying both, of both kinds, on both sides, about, around.
amphigonic: Pertaining to amphigony; sexual; as, amphigonic propagation.
amuletic: Of or pertaining to an amulet; operating as a charm.
amortization: 1. (Law) The act or right of alienating lands to a corporation, which was considered formerly as transferring them to dead hands, or in mortmain. 2. The extinction of a debt, usually by means of a sinking fund; also, the money thus paid. Simmonds.
amygdalic: Of or pertaining to almonds; derived from amygdalin; as, amygdalic acid.
ampere: The unit of electric current; -- defined by the International Electrical Congress in 1893 and by U. S. Statute as, one tenth of the unit of current of the C. G. S. | The unit of electric current; -- defined by the International Electrical Congress in 1893 and by U. S. Statute as, one tenth of the unit of current of the C. G. S.
amphiaster: The achromatic figure, formed in mitotic cell-division, consisting of two asters connected by a spindle-shaped bundle of rodlike fibers diverging from each aster, and called the spindle.
amphigen: An element that in combination produces amphid salt; -- applied by Berzelius to oxygen, sulphur, selenium, and tellurium.
amiable: 1. Lovable; lovely; pleasing. [Obs. or R.] So amiable a prospect. Sir T. Herbert. 2. Friendly; kindly; sweet; gracious; as, an amiable temper or mood; amiable ideas. 3. Possessing sweetness of disposition; having sweetness of temper, kind-heartedness, etc., which causes one to be liked; as, an amiable woman. 4. Done out of love.
ammonitoidea: An extensive group of fossil cephalopods often very abundant in Mesozoic rocks. See Ammonite.
amperefoot: A unit, employed in calculating fall of pressure in distributing mains, equivalent to a current of one ampère flowing through one foot of conductor.
amain: 1. With might; with full force; vigorously; violently; exceedingly. They on the hill, which were not yet come to blows, perceiving the fewness of their enemies, came down amain. Milton. | To lower, as a sail, a yard, etc.
amboynabutton: A chronic contagious affection of the skin, prevalent in the tropics.
amarantaceous: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, the family of plants of which the amaranth is the type.
amate: To dismay; to dishearten; to daunt. [Obs. or Archaic] The Silures, to amate the new general, rumored the overthrow greater than was true. Milton. | To be a mate to; to match. (old) Spenser.
ambassage: Same as Embassage. [Obs. or R.] Luke xiv. 32.
amorwe: 1. In the morning. (old) Chaucer. 2. On the following morning. (old) Chaucer.
amercement: The infliction of a penalty at the discretion of the court; also, a mulct or penalty thus imposed. It differs from a fine,in that the latter is, or was originally, a fixed and certain sum prescribed by statue for an offense; but an amercement is arbitrary. Hence, the act or practice of affeering. [See Affeer.] Blackstone. Note: This word, in old books, is written amerciament.
amelcorn: A variety of wheat from which starch is produced; -- called also French rice.
amethyst: 1. (Min.) A variety of crystallized quartz, of a purple or bluish violet color, of different shades. It is much used as a jeweler's stone. Oriental amethyst, the violet-blue variety of transparent crystallized corundum or sapphire. 2. (Her.) A purple color in a nobleman's escutcheon, or coat of arms.
amphiblastic: Segmenting unequally; -- said of telolecithal ova with complete segmentation.
amongst: 1. Mixed or mingled; surrounded by. They heard, And from his presence hid themselves among The thickest trees. Milton. 2. Conjoined, or associated with, or making part of the number of; in the number or class of. Blessed art thou among women. Luke i. 28. 3. Expressing a relation of dispersion, distribution, etc.; also, a relation of reciprocal action.
ampulla: 1. (Rom. Antiq.) A narrow-necked vessel having two handles and bellying out like a jug. 2. (Eccl.) (a) A cruet for the wine and water at Mass. (b) The vase in which the holy oil for chrism, unction, or coronation is kept. Shipley. 3. (Biol.) Any membranous bag shaped like a leathern bottle, as the dilated end of a vessel or duct;
amusing: Giving amusement; diverting; as, an amusing story. -- A*mus"ing*ly, adv.
amanita: A genus of poisonous fungi of the family Agaricaceæ, characterized by having a volva, an annulus, and white spores. The species resemble edible mushrooms, and are frequently mistaken for them. Amanita muscaria, syn. Agaricus muscarius, is the fly amanita, or fly agaric; and A. phalloides is the death cup.
ambidextrousness: The quality of being ambidextrous; ambidexterity.
amalgama: Same as Amalgam. They divided this their amalgama into a number of incoherent republics. Burke.
amphibole: A common mineral embracing many varieties varying in color and in composition. It occurs in monoclinic crystals; also massive, generally with fibrous or columnar structure. The color varies from white to gray, green, brown, and black. It is a silicate of magnesium and calcium, with usually aluminium and iron.
ambiguous: Doubtful or uncertain, particularly in respect to signification; capable of being understood in either of two or more possible senses; equivocal; as, an ambiguous course; an ambiguous expression. What have been thy answers What but dark, Ambiguous, and with double sense deluding Milton. Syn. -- Doubtful; dubious; uncertain; unsettled; indistinct; indeterminate; indefinite.
amphigenous: Increasing in size by growth on all sides, as the lichens.
amaurotic: Affected with amaurosis; having the characteristics of amaurosis.
amadavat: The strawberry finch, a small Indian song bird (Estrelda amandava), commonly caged and kept for fighting. The female is olive brown; the male, in summer, mostly crimson; -- called also red waxbill. [Written also amaduvad and avadavat.]
ambitious: 1. Possessing, or controlled by, ambition; greatly or inordinately desirous of power, honor, office, superiority, or distinction. Yet Brutus says he was ambitious, And Brutus is an honorable man. Shak. 2. Strongly desirous; -- followed by of or the infinitive; as, ambitious to be or to do something. I was not ambitious of seeing this ceremony. Evelyn.
amazonstone: A variety of feldspar, having a verdigris-green color.
amphipneust: One of a tribe of Amphibia, which have both lungs and gills at the same time, as the proteus and siren.
amnigenous: Born or bred in, of, or near a river. (old) Bailey.
amanitine: The poisonous principle of some fungi.
amplify: 1. To render larger, more extended, or more intense, and the like; -- used especially of telescopes, microscopes, etc. 2. (Rhet.) To enlarge by addition or discussion; | 1. To become larger. (old) Strait was the way at first, withouten light, But further in did further amplify. Fairfax. 2. To speak largely or copiously; to be diffuse in argument or description;
ambilevous: Left-handed on both sides; clumsy; -- opposed to ambidexter. Sir T. Browne.
amelioration: The act of ameliorating, or the state of being ameliorated; making or becoming better; improvement; melioration. "Amelioration of human affairs." J. S. Mill.
ambulatory: 1. Of or pertaining to walking; having the faculty of walking; formed or fitted for walking; as, an ambulatory animal. 2. Accustomed to move from place to place; not stationary; movable; | A place to walk in, whether in the open air, as the gallery of a cloister, or within a building.
amphiarthrosis: A form of articulation in which the bones are connected by intervening substance admitting slight motion; symphysis.
ambertree: A species of Anthospermum, a shrub with evergreen leaves, which, when bruised, emit a fragrant odor.
amalgamator: One who, or that which, amalgamates. Specifically: A machine for separating precious metals from earthy particles by bringing them in contact with a body of mercury with which they form an amalgam.
amblypoda: A group of large, extinct, herbivorous mammals, common in the Tertiary formation of the United States.
amazement: 1. The condition of being amazed; bewilderment (old); overwhelming wonder, as from surprise, sudden fear, horror, or admiration. His words impression left Of much amazement. Milton. 2. Frenzy; madness. (old) Webster (1661).
amygdaline: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, almonds.
ammonium: A compound radical, NH4, having the chemical relations of a strongly basic element like the alkali metals.
amphibiotica: A division of insects having aquatic larvæ.
amianthus: Earth flax, or mountain flax; a soft silky variety of asbestus.
amblygon: An obtuse-angled figure, esp. and obtuse-angled triangle. (old)
amaranth: 1. An imaginary flower supposed never to fade. (poetic) 2. (Bot.) A genus of ornamental annual plants (Amaranthus) of many species, with green, purplish, or crimson flowers. 2. A color inclining to purple.
amphiprostyle: Doubly prostyle; having columns at each end, but not at the sides. -- n. An amphiprostyle temple or edifice.
ametabolous: Not undergoing any metamorphosis; as, ametabolic insects.
amotion: 1. Removal; ousting; especially, the removal of a corporate officer from his office. 2. Deprivation of possession.
amphora: Among the ancients, a two-handled vessel, tapering at the bottom, used for holding wine, oil, etc.
amateur: A person attached to a particular pursuit, study, or science as to music or painting; esp. one who cultivates any study or art, from taste or attachment, without pursuing it professionally.
ambary: A valuable East Indian fiber plant (Hibiscus cannabinus), or its fiber, which is used throughout India for making ropes, cordage, and a coarse canvas and sackcloth; --called also brown Indian hemp.
ambidexterity: 1. The quality of being ambidexas, ambidexterity of argumentation. Sterne. Ignorant I was of the human frame, and of its latent powers, as regarded speed, force, and ambidexterity. De Quincey. 2. Double-dealing. (Law) A juror's taking of money from the both parties for a verdict.
ambrosiac: Having the qualities of ambrosia; delicious. "Ambrosiac odors." B. Jonson.
amidol: A salt of a diamino phenol, C6H3(OH)(NH2)2, used as a developer.
amity: Friendship, in a general sense, between individuals, societies, or nations; friendly relations; good understanding; as, a treaty of amity and commerce; the amity of the Whigs and Tories. To live on terms of amity with vice. Cowper. Syn. -- Harmony; friendliness; friendship; affection; good will; peace.
amorphous: 1. Having no determinate form; of irregular; shapeless. Kirwan. 2. Without crystallization in the ultimate texture of a solid substance; uncrystallized. 3. Of no particular kind or character; anomalous. Scientific treatises . . . are not seldom rude and amorphous in style. Hare. -- A*mor"phous*ly, adv. -- A*mor"phous*ness, n.
amphirhina: A name applied to the elasmobranch fishes, because the nasal sac is double.
amphimacer: A foot of three syllables, the middle one short and the others long, as in cast. Andrews.
amphisbaena: 1. A fabled serpent with a head at each end, moving either way. Milton. 2. (Zoöl.) A genus of harmless lizards, serpentlike in form, without legs, and with both ends so much alike that they appear to have a head at each, and ability to move either way. See Illustration in Appendix. Note: The Gordius aquaticus, or hairworm, has been called an amphisbæna;
ambury: 1. (Far.) A soft tumor or bloody wart on horses or oxen. 2. A disease of the roots of turnips, etc.; -- called also fingers and toes.
amalgamation: 1. The act or operation of compounding mercury with another metal; -- applied particularly to the process of separating gold and silver from their ores by mixing them with mercury. Ure. 2. The mixing or blending of different elements, races, societies, etc.; also, the result of such combination or blending; a homogeneous union. Macaulay.
ampyx: A woman's headband (sometimes of metal), for binding the front hair.
amylolytic: Effecting the conversion of starch into soluble dextrin and sugar; as, an amylolytic ferment. Foster.
amphitrocha: A kind of annelid larva having both a dorsal and a ventral circle of special cilia.
ambassadress: A female ambassador; also, the wife of an ambassador. Prescott.
ambreate: A salt formed by the combination of ambreic acid with a base or positive radical.
amice: A square of white linen worn at first on the head, but now about the neck and shoulders, by priests of the Roman Catholic Church while saying Mass. | A hood, or cape with a hood, made of lined with gray fur, formerly worn by the clergy; -- written also amess, amyss, and almuce.
amiss: Astray; faultily; improperly; wrongly; ill. What error drives our eyes and ears amiss Shak. Ye ask and receive not, because ye ask amiss. James iv. 3. To take (an act, thing) amiss, to impute a wrong… | Wrong; faulty; out of order; improper; as, it may not be amiss to ask advice. Note: [Used only in the predicate.] Dryden. His wisdom and virtue can not always rectify that which is amiss in himself…
amentaceous: (a) Resembling, or consisting of, an ament or aments; as, the chestnut has an amentaceous inflorescence. (b) Bearing aments; having flowers arranged in aments; as, amentaceous plants.
amove: 1. To remove, as a person or thing, from a position. (old) Dr. H. More. 2. (Law) To dismiss from an office or station. | To move or be moved; to excite. (old) Spenser.
amorousness: The quality of being amorous, or inclined to sexual love; lovingness.
amuck: In a frenzied and reckless. To run amuck, to rush out in a state of frenzy, as the Malays sometimes do under the influence of "bhang," and attack every one that comes in the way; to assail recklessly and indiscriminately. Satire's my weapon, but I'm too discreet To run amuck, and tilt at all I meet. Pope.
amphiboly: Ambiguous discourse; amphibology. If it oracle contrary to our interest or humor, we will create an amphiboly, a double meaning where there is none. Whitlock.
amphicoelian: Having both ends concave; biconcave; -- said of vertebræ.
amende: A pecuniary punishment or fine; a reparation or recantation. Amende honorable(#). (Old French Law) A species of infamous punishment in which the offender, being led into court with a rope about his neck, and a lighted torch in his hand, begged pardon of his God, the court, etc.
amendable: Capable of being amended; as, an amendable writ or error. -- A*mend"a*ble*ness, n.
amorous: 1. Inclined to love; having a propensity to love, or to sexual enjoyment; loving; fond; affectionate; as, an amorous disposition. 2. Affected with love; in love; enamored; -- usually with of; formerly with on. Thy roses amorous of the moon. Keats. High nature amorous of the good. Tennyson. Sure my brother is amorous on Hero. Shak. 3. Of or relating to, or produced by, love.
ambuscade: 1. A lying in a wood, concealed, for the purpose of attacking an enemy by surprise. Hence: A lying in wait, and concealed in any situation, for a like purpose; a snare laid for an enemy; an ambush. | 1. To post or conceal in ambush; to ambush. 2. To lie in wait for, or to attack from a covert or lurking place; to waylay.
amit: To lose. (old) A lodestone fired doth presently amit its proper virtue. Sir T. Browne.
amadou: A spongy, combustible substance, prepared from fungus (Boletus and Polyporus) which grows on old trees; German tinder; punk. It has been employed as a styptic by surgeons, but its common use is as tinder, for which purpose it is prepared by soaking it in a strong solution of niter. Ure.
amplexicaul: Clasping or embracing a stem, as the base of some leaves. Gray.
amass: To collect into a mass or heap; to gather a great quantity of; to accumulate; as, to amass a treasure or a fortune; to amass words or phrases. The life Homer has been written by amassing all the… | A mass; a heap. (old) Sir H. Wotton.
amberfish: A fish of the southern Atlantic coast (Seriola Carolinensis.)
ambulacral: Of or pertaining to ambulacra; avenuelike; as, the ambulacral ossicles, plates, spines, and suckers of echinoderms.
ambrose: A sweet-scented herb; ambrosia. See Ambrosia, 3. Turner.
amphistylic: Having the mandibular arch articulated with the hyoid arch and the cranium, as in the cestraciont sharks; -- said of a skull.
amphopeptone: A product of gastric digestion, a mixture of hemipeptone and antipeptone.
amylolysis: The conversion of starch into soluble products, as dextrins and sugar, esp. by the action of enzymes. -- Am`y*lo*lyt"ic (#), a.
amphibrach: A foot of three syllables, the middle one long, the first and last short (as, h. In modern prosody the accented syllable takes the place of the long and the unaccented of the short; as, pro-phet''ic.
ambsace: Double aces, the lowest throw of all at dice. Hence: Bad luck; anything of no account or value.
amortizable: Capable of being cleared off, as a debt.
amphipodous: Of or pertaining to the Amphipoda.
amnesic: Of or pertaining to amnesia. "Amnesic or coördinate defects." Quian.
ambulant: Walking; moving from place to place. Gayton.
amphibolic: 1. Of or pertaining to amphiboly; ambiguous; equivocal. 2. Of or resembling the mineral amphibole.
am: The first person singular of the verb be, in the indicative mode, present tense. See Be. God said unto Moses, I am that am. Exod. iii. 14.
amoeboid: Resembling an amoeba; amoeba-shaped; changing in shape like an amoeba. Amoeboid movement, movement produced, as in the amoeba, by successive processes of prolongation and retraction.
amioidei: An order of ganoid fishes of which Amis is type. See Bowfin and Ganoidei.
amassette: An instrument of horn used for collecting painters' colors on the stone in the process of grinding.
amort: As if dead; lifeless; spiritless; dejected; depressed. Shak.
ambo: A large pulpit or reading desk, in the early Christian churches. Gwilt.
amphibiology: A treatise on amphibious animals; the department of natural history which treats of the Amphibia.
ameliorate: To make better; to improve; to meliorate. In every human being there is a wish to ameliorate his own condition. Macaulay. | To grow better; to meliorate; as, wine ameliorates by age.
amylnitrite: A yellowish oily volatile liquid, C5H11NO2, used in medicine as a heart stimulant and a vasodilator. The inhalation of its vapor instantly produces flushing of the face.
ambigu: An entertainment at which a medley of dishes is set on at the same time.
aminol: A colorless liquid prepared from herring brine and containing amines, used as a local antiseptic.
amanuensis: A person whose employment is to write what another dictates, or to copy what another has written.
amensaetthoro: A kind of divorce which does not dissolve the marriage bond, but merely authorizes a separate life of the husband and wife. Abbott.
ambergris: A substance of the consistence of wax, found floating in the Indian Ocean and other parts of the tropics, and also as a morbid secretion in the intestines of the sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus), which is believed to be in all cases its true origin. In color it is white, ash-gray, yellow, or black, and often variegated like marble.
amphicome: A kind of figured stone, rugged and beset with eminences, anciently used in divination. (old) Encyc. Brit.
ambrotype: A picture taken on a place of prepared glass, in which the lights are represented in silver, and the shades are produced by a dark background visible through the unsilvered portions of the glass.
amour: 1. Love; affection. (old) 2. Love making; a love affair; usually, an unlawful connection in love; a love intrigue; an illicit love affair. In amours with, in love with. (old)
ambrosiabeetle: A bark beetle that feeds on ambrosia.
amphictyony: A league of states of ancient Greece; esp. the celebrated confederation known as the Amphictyonic Council. Its object was to maintain the common interests of Greece.
amberseed: Seed of the Hibiscus abelmoschus, somewhat resembling millet, brought from Egypt and the West Indies, and having a flavor like that of musk; musk seed. Chambers.
amphictyons: Deputies from the confederated states of ancient Greece to a congress or council. They considered both political and religious matters.
amarine: A characteristic crystalline substance, obtained from oil of bitter almonds.
amygdalaceous: Akin to, or derived from, the almond.
amphitheatrically: In the form or manner of an amphitheater.
amount: 1. To go up; to ascend. (old) So up he rose, and thence amounted straight. Spenser. 2. To rise or reach by an accumulation of particular sums or quantities; to come (to) in the aggregate or whole; | To signify; to amount to. (old)
ambiguity: The quality or state of being ambiguous; doubtfulness or uncertainty, particularly as to the signification of language, arising from its admitting of more than one meaning; an equivocal word or expression. No shadow of ambiguity can rest upon the course to be pursued. I. Taylor. The words are of single signification, without any ambiguity. South.
amphidromical: Pertaining to an Attic festival at the naming of a child; -- so called because the friends of the parents carried the child around the hearth and then named it.
amend: To change or modify in any way for the better; as, (a) by simply removing what is erroneous, corrupt, superfluous, faulty, and the like; (b) by supplying deficiencies; | To grow better by rectifying something wrong in manners or morals; to improve. "My fortune . . . amends." Sir P. Sidney.
amatory: Pertaining to, producing, or expressing, sexual love; as, amatory potions.
ample: Large; great in size, extent, capacity, or bulk; spacious; roomy; widely extended. All the people in that ample house Did to that image bow their humble knees. Spenser. 2. Fully sufficient; abundant; liberal; copious; as, an ample fortune; ample justice. 3. Not contracted of brief; not concise; extended; diffusive; as, an ample narrative. Johnson. Syn. -- Full; spacious;
ambaryhemp: A valuable East Indian fiber plant (Hibiscus cannabinus), or its fiber, which is used throughout India for making ropes, cordage, and a coarse canvas and sackcloth; --called also brown Indian hemp.
ampereturn: A unit equal to the product of one complete convolution (of a coiled conductor) into one ampère of current; thus, a conductor having five convolutions and carrying a current of half an ampère is said to have 2½ ampère turns. The magnetizing effect of a coil is proportional to the number of its ampère turns.
amblyopia: Weakness of sight, without and opacity of the cornea, or of the interior of the eye; the first degree of amaurosis.
amylic: Pertaining to, or derived from, amyl; as, amylic ether. Amylic alcohol (Chem.), one of the series of alcohols, a transparent, colorless liquid, having a peculiar odor. It is the hydroxide of amyl. -- Amylic fermentation (Chem.), a process of fermentation in starch or sugar in which amylic alcohol is produced. Gregory.
amygdala: 1. An almond. 2. (Anat.) (a) One of the tonsils of the pharynx. (b) One of the rounded prominences of the lower surface of the lateral hemispheres of the cerebellum, each side of the vallecula.
amphineura: A division of Mollusca remarkable for the bilateral symmetry of the organs and the arrangement of the nerves.
amt: An administrative territorial division in Denmark and Norway. Each of the provinces [of Denmark] is divided into several amts, answering . . . to the English hundreds. Encyc. Brit.
ambreic: Of or pertaining to ambrein; -- said of a certain acid produced by digesting ambrein in nitric acid.
amen: An expression used at the end of prayers, and meaning, So be it. At the end of a creed, it is a solemn asseveration of belief. When it introduces a declaration, it is equivalent to truly, verily. | To say Amen to; to sanction fully.
amperemeter: An instrument for measuring the strength of an electrical current in ampères.
ambidextrous: 1. Pertaining the faculty of using both hands with equal ease. Sir T. Browne. 2. Practicing or siding with both parties. All false, shuffling, and ambidextrous dealings. L'Estrange.
amitotic: Of or pertaining to amitosis; karyostenotic; -- opposed to mitotic.
ambrite: A fossil resin occurring in large masses in New Zealand.
ambassador: 1. A minister of the highest rank sent a foreign court to represent there his sovereign or country. Note: Ambassador are either ordinary [or resident] or extraordinary, that is, sent upon some special or unusual occasion or errand. Abbott. 2. An official messenger and representative.
amidin: Start modified by heat so as to become a transparent mass, like horn. It is soluble in cold water.
amphid: A salt of the class formed by the combination of an acid and a base, or by the union of two oxides, two sulphides, selenides, or tellurides, as distinguished from a haloid compound. Berzelius.
amble: 1. To go at the easy gait called an amble; -- applied to the horse or to its rider. 2. To move somewhat like an ambling horse; to go easily or without hard shocks. | 1. A peculiar gait of a horse, in which both legs on the same side are moved at the same time, alternating with the legs on the other side. "A fine easy amble." B. Jonson. 2.
ambrosially: After the manner of ambrosia; delightfully. "Smelt ambrosially." Tennyson.
amphisbaenoid: Like or pertaining to the lizards of the genus Amphisbæna.
amperehour: The quantity of electricity delivered in one hour by a current whose average strength is one ampère. It is used as a unit of quantity, and is equal to 3600 coulombs. The terms Ampère minute and Ampère second are sometimes similarly used.
ammite: Oölite or roestone; -- written also hammite. (old)
amberroom: A room formerly in the Czar's Summer Palace in Russia, which was richly decorated with walls and fixtures made from amber. The amber was removed by occupying German troops during the Second World War and has, as of 1997, never been recovered. The room is being recreated from old photographs by Russian artisans. PJC
amylometer: Instrument for determining the amount of starch in a substance.
amphictyonic: Of or pertaining to the Amphictyons or their League or Council; as, an Amphictyonic town or state; the Amphictyonic body. W. Smith.
amylobacter: A microörganism (Bacillus amylobacter) which develops in vegetable tissue during putrefaction. Sternberg.
amnicolist: One who lives near a river. (old) Bailey.
amvis: An explosive consisting of ammonium nitrate, a derivative of nitrobenzene, chlorated napthalene, and wood meal.
amiability: The quality of being amiable; amiableness; sweetness of disposition. Every excellency is a degree of amiability. Jer. Taylor.
amylate: A compound of the radical amyl with oxygen and a positive atom or radical.
amphidisc: A peculiar small siliceous spicule having a denticulated wheel at each end; -- found in freshwater sponges.
amazedly: In amazement; with confusion or astonishment. Shak.
ambrosia: 1. (Myth.) (a) The fabled food of the gods (as nectar was their drink), which conferred immortality upon those who partook of it. (b) An unguent of the gods. His dewy locks distilled ambrosia. Milton. 2. A perfumed unguent, salve, or draught; something very pleasing to the taste or smell. Spenser. 3. Formerly, a kind of fragrant plant;
ametabolian: Of or pertaining to insects that do undergo any metamorphosis.
amenableness: The quality or state of being amenable; liability to answer charges; answerableness.
amber: 1. (Min.) A yellowish translucent resin resembling copal, found as a fossil in alluvial soils, with beds of lignite, or on the seashore in many places. It takes a fine polish, and is used for pipe… | 1. Consisting of amber; made of amber. "Amber bracelets." Shak. 2. Resembling amber, especially in color; amber-colored. "The amber morn." Tennyson.
ampersand: A word used to describe the character Halliwell.
amphitheatre: 1. An oval or circular building with rising tiers of seats about an open space called the arena. Note: The Romans first constructed amphitheaters for combats of gladiators and wild beasts. 2. Anything resembling an amphitheater in form; as, a level surrounded by rising slopes or hills, or a rising gallery in a theater.
amputate: 1. To prune or lop off, as branches or tendrils. 2. (Surg.) To cut off (a limb or projecting part (of the body). Wiseman.
amylopsin: The diastase of the pancreatic juice.
amphibolous: 1. Ambiguous; doubtful. (old) Never was there such an amphibolous quarrel -- both parties declaring themselves for the king. Howell. 2. (Logic) Capable of two meanings. An amphibolous sentence is one that is capable of two meanings, not from the double sense of any of the words, but from its admitting of a double construction; e.
ampelite: An earth abounding in pyrites, used by the ancients to kill insects, etc., on vines; -- applied by Brongniart to a carbonaceous alum schist.
amphipod: Of or pertaining to the Amphipoda.
american: 1. Of or pertaining to America; as, the American continent: American Indians. 2. Of or pertaining to the United States. "A young officer of the American navy." Lyell. American ivy. | A native of America; -- originally applied to the aboriginal inhabitants, but now applied to the descendants of Europeans born in America, and especially to the citizens of the United States.
amygdaloid: A variety of trap or basaltic rock, containing small cavities, occupied, wholly or in part, by nodules or geodes of different minerals, esp. agates, quartz, calcite, and the zeolites. | 1. Almond-shaped. 2. Pertaining to, or having the nature of, the rock amygdaloid.
ambidexter: Using both hands with equal ease. Smollett. | 1. A person who uses both hands with equal facility. 2. Hence; A double-dealer; one equally ready to act on either side in party disputes. The rest are hypocrites, ambidexters, so many turning…
amidst: In the midst or middle of; surrounded or encompassed by; among. "This fair tree amidst the garden." "Unseen amid the throng." "Amidst thick clouds." Milton. "Amidst acclamations." "Amidst the splendor and festivity of a court." Macaulay. But rather famish them amid their plenty. Shak. Syn. -- Amidst, Among.
amphipoda: A numerous group of fourteen -- footed Crustacea, inhabiting both fresh and salt water. The body is usually compressed laterally, and the anterior pairs or legs are directed downward and forward, but the posterior legs are usually turned upward and backward. The beach flea is an example. See Tetradecapoda and Arthrostraca.
amorphozoa: Animals without a mouth or regular internal organs, as the sponges.
amicability: The quality of being amicable; friendliness; amicableness. Ash.
ametabolic: Not undergoing any metamorphosis; as, ametabolic insects.
amygdalate: Pertaining to, resembling, or made of, almonds. | 1. (Med.) An emulsion made of almonds; milk of almonds. Bailey. Coxe. 2. (Chem.) A salt amygdalic acid.
amplifier: One who or that which amplifies.
amblyopy: Weakness of sight, without and opacity of the cornea, or of the interior of the eye; the first degree of amaurosis.
amoebea: That division of the Rhizopoda which includes the amoeba and similar forms.
amaryllis: 1. A pastoral sweetheart. To sport with Amaryllis in the shade. Milton. 2. (bot.) (a) A family of plants much esteemed for their beauty, including the narcissus, jonquil, daffodil, agave, and others. (b) A genus of the same family, including the Belladonna lily.
amusette: A light field cannon, or stocked gun mounted on a swivel.
amphitropal: Having the ovule inverted, but with the attachment near the middle of one side; half anatropous.
ampelopsis: A genus formerly including the Virginia creeper.
amperesecond: The quantity of electricity delivered in one hour by a current whose average strength is one ampère. It is used as a unit of quantity, and is equal to 3600 coulombs. The terms Ampère minute and Ampère second are sometimes similarly used.
amusement: 1. Deep thought; muse. (old) Here I . . . fell into a strong and deep amusement, revolving in my mind, with great perplexity, the amazing change of our affairs. Fleetwood. 2. The state of being amused; pleasurable excitement; that which amuses; diversion. His favorite amusements were architecture and gardening. Macaulay. Syn. -- Diversion; entertainment; recreation;
ampullaceous: Like a bottle or inflated bladder; bottle-shaped; swelling. Kirby. Ampullaceous sac (Zoöl.), one of the peculiar cavities in the tissues of sponges, containing the zooidal cells.
ammonite: A fossil cephalopod shell related to the nautilus. There are many genera and species, and all are extinct, the typical forms having existed only in the Mesozoic age, when they were exceedingly numerous. They differ from the nautili in having the margins of the septa very much lobed or plaited, and the siphuncle dorsal. Also called serpent stone, snake stone, and cornu Ammonis.
amplexation: An embrace. (old) An humble amplexation of those sacred feet. Bp. Hall.
ambit: Circuit or compass. His great parts did not live within a small ambit. Milward.
amorphozoic: Of or pertaining to the Amorphozoa.
amassment: An amassing; a heap collected; a large quantity or number brought together; an accumulation. An amassment of imaginary conceptions. Glanvill.
amphiuma: A genus of amphibians, inhabiting the Southern United States, having a serpentlike form, but with four minute limbs and two persistent gill openings; the Congo snake.
amphoral: Pertaining to, or resembling, an amphora.
amicableness: The quality of being amicable; amicability.
amandine: 1. The vegetable casein of almonds. 2. A kind of cold cream prepared from almonds, for chapped hands, etc.
amateurism: The practice, habit, or work of an amateur.
amability: Lovableness. Jer. Taylor. Note: The New English Dictionary (Murray) says this word is "usefully distinct from Amiability."
amputation: The act amputating; esp. the operation of cutting of a limb or projecting part of the body.
ambulate: To walk; to move about. Southey.
amess: Amice, a hood or cape. See 2d Amice.
amphicarpous: Producing fruit of two kinds, either as to form or time of ripening.
amyloidal: Resembling or containing amyl; starchlike. Amyloid degeneration (Med.), a diseased condition of various organs of the body, produced by the deposit of an albuminous substance, giving a blue color with iodine and sulphuric acid; -- called also waxy or lardaceous degeneration.
ambiparous: Characterized by containing the rudiments of both flowers and leaves; -- applied to a bud.
amboynapine: The resiniferous tree Agathis Dammara, of the Moluccas.
ambrein: A fragrant substance which is the chief constituent of ambergris.
amenity: The quality of being pleasant or agreeable, whether in respect to situation, climate, manners, or disposition; pleasantness; civility; suavity; gentleness. A sweetness and amenity of temper. Buckle. This climate has not seduced by its amenities. W. Howitt.
amphiscii: The inhabitants of the tropic, whose shadows in one part of the year are cast to the north, and in the other to the south, according as the sun is south or north of their zenith.
ammonia: A gaseous compound of hydrogen and nitrogen, NH3, with a pungent smell and taste: -- often called volatile alkali, and spirits of hartshorn.
amorist: A lover; a gallant. Milton. It was the custom for an amorist to impress the name of his mistress in the dust, or upon the damp earth, with letters fixed upon his shoe. Southey.
amaryllideous: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, an order of plants differing from the lily family chiefly in having the ovary below the
amphigoric: Nonsensical; absurd; pertaining to an amphigory.
americanize: To render American; to assimilate to the Americans in customs, ideas, etc.; to stamp with American characteristics.
amphibology: A phrase, discourse, or proposition, susceptible of two interpretations; and hence, of uncertain meaning. It differs from equivocation, which arises from the twofold sense of a single term.
amaryllidaceous: Of, pertaining to, or resembling, an order of plants differing from the lily family chiefly in having the ovary below the
amb: A prefix meaning about, around; -- used in words derived from the Latin.
amissibility: The quality of being amissible; possibility of being lost. Notions of popular rights and the amissibility of sovereign power for misconduct were alternately broached by the two great religious parties of Europe. Hallam.
amolition: Removal; a putting away. (old) Bp. Ward (1673).
ameer: 1. Emir. (old) 2. One of the Mohammedan nobility of Afghanistan and Scinde.
amphigean: Extending over all the zones, from the tropics to the polar zones inclusive.
amyloid: 1. A non-nitrogenous starchy food; a starchlike substance. 2. (Med.) The substance deposited in the organs in amyloid degeneration. | Resembling or containing amyl; starchlike. Amyloid degeneration (Med.), a diseased condition of various organs of the body, produced by the deposit of an albuminous substance, giving a blue color…
ammeter: A contraction of amperometer or ampèremeter.
ampliation: 1. Enlargement; amplification. 2. (Civil Law) A postponement of the decision of a cause, for further consideration or re-argument.
ambulacrum: (a) One of the radical zones of echinoderms, along which run the principal nerves, blood vessels, and water tubes. These zones usually bear rows of locomotive suckers or tentacles, which protrude from regular pores. In star fishes they occupy the grooves along the under side of the rays. (b) One of the suckers on the feet of mites.
amoeba: A rhizopod. common in fresh water, capable of undergoing many changes of form at will. See Rhizopoda.
amotus: Elevated, -- as a toe, when raised so high that the tip does not touch the ground.
amphibia: One of the classes of vertebrates. Note: The Amphibia are distinguished by having usually no scales, by having eggs and embryos similar to those of fishes, and by undergoing a complete metamorphosis, the young having gills. There are three living orders: (1) The tailless, as the frogs (Anura);
amyss: Same as Amice, a hood or cape.
ambidextral: Pertaining equally to the right-hand side and the left-hand side. Earle.
ampliative: Enlarging a conception by adding to that which is already known or received. "All bodies possess power of attraction" is an ampliative judgment; because we can think of bodies without thinking of attraction as one of their immediate primary attribute. Abp. W. Thomson.
amylogenic: 1. Of or pert. to amylogen. 2. Forming starch; -- applied specif. to leucoplasts.
amuse: 1. To occupy or engage the attention of; to lose in deep thought; to absorb; also, to distract; to bewilder. (old) Camillus set upon the Gauls when they were amused in receiving their gold. Holland. Being amused with grief, fear, and fright, he could not find the house. Fuller. 2. To entertain or occupy in a pleasant manner; to stir with pleasing or mirthful emotions;
amphitropous: Having the ovule inverted, but with the attachment near the middle of one side; half anatropous.
amaurosis: A loss or decay of sight, from loss of power in the optic nerve, without any perceptible external change in the eye; -- called also gutta serena, the "drop serene" of Milton.
amphicarpic: Producing fruit of two kinds, either as to form or time of ripening.
ambler: A horse or a person that ambles.
amasthenic: Uniting the chemical rays of light into one focus, as a certain kind of lens; amacratic.
ambulance: (a) A field hospital, so organized as to follow an army in its movements, and intended to succor the wounded as soon as possible. Often used adjectively; as, an ambulance wagon; ambulance stretcher; ambulance corps. (b) An ambulance wagon or cart for conveying the wounded from the field, or to a hospital.
amylalcohol: Any of eight isomeric liquid compounds, C5H11OH; ordinarily, a mixture of two of these forming a colorless liquid with a peculiar cough-exciting odor and burning taste, the chief constituent of fusel oil. It is used as a source of amyl compounds, such as amyl acetate, amyl nitrite, etc.
amortize: 1. To make as if dead; to destroy. (old) Chaucer. 2. (Law) To alienate in mortmain, that is, to convey to a corporation. See Mortmain. 3. To clear off or extinguish, as a debt, usually by means of a sinking fund.
amide: A compound formed by the union of amidogen with an acid element or radical. It may also be regarded as ammonia in which one or more hydrogen atoms have been replaced by an acid atom or radical. Acid amide, a neutral compound formed by the substitution of the amido group for hydroxyl in an acid.
ammoniacal: Of or pertaining to ammonia, or possessing its properties; as, an ammoniac salt; ammoniacal gas. amaranthine: 1. Of or pertaining to amaranth. "Amaranthine bowers." Pope. 2. Unfading, as the poetic amaranth; undying. They only amaranthine flower on earth Is virtue. Cowper. 3. Of a purplish color. Buchanan.
ambassade: 1. The mission of an ambassador. (old) Carew. 2. An embassy. (old) Strype.
amativeness: The faculty supposed to influence sexual desire; propensity to love. Combe.
amornings: In the morning; every morning. (old) And have such pleasant walks into the woods A-mornings. J. Fletcher.
amendment: 1. An alteration or change for the better; correction of a fault or of faults; reformation of life by quitting vices. 2. In public bodies; Any alternation made or proposed to be made in a bill or motion by adding, changing, substituting, or omitting. 3. (Law) Correction of an error in a writ or process. Syn. -- Improvement; reformation; emendation.
amphipodan: Of or pertaining to the Amphipoda.
amperage: The strength of a current of electricity carried by a conductor or generated by a machine, measured in ampères.
amorosa: A wanton woman; a courtesan. Sir T. Herbert.
amphicoelous: Having both ends concave; biconcave; -- said of vertebræ.
amperometer: An instrument for measuring the strength of an electrical current in ampères.
amphoteric: Partly one and partly the other; neither acid nor alkaline; neutral. Smart.
amethystine: 1. Resembling amethyst, especially in color; bluish violet. 2. Composed of, or containing, amethyst.
amygdaloidal: 1. Almond-shaped. 2. Pertaining to, or having the nature of, the rock amygdaloid.
amic: Related to, or derived, ammonia; -- used chiefly as a suffix; as, amic acid; phosphamic acid. Amic acid (Chem.), one of a class of nitrogenized acids somewhat resembling amides.
ambulator: 1. One who walks about; a walker. 2. (Zoöl.) (a) A beetle of the genus Lamia. (b) A genus of birds, or one of this genus. 3. An instrument for measuring distances; -- called also perambulator. Knight.
amphitheater: 1. An oval or circular building with rising tiers of seats about an open space called the arena. Note: The Romans first constructed amphitheaters for combats of gladiators and wild beasts. 2. Anything resembling an amphitheater in form; as, a level surrounded by rising slopes or hills, or a rising gallery in a theater.
ampleness: The state or quality of being ample; largeness; fullness; completeness.
ampereminute: The quantity of electricity delivered in one hour by a current whose average strength is one ampère. It is used as a unit of quantity, and is equal to 3600 coulombs. The terms Ampère minute and Ampère second are sometimes similarly used.
amphitheatric: Of, pertaining to, exhibited in, or resembling, an amphitheater.
amplification: 1. The act of amplifying or enlarging in dimensions; enlargement; extension. 2. (Rhet.) The enlarging of a simple statement by particularity of description, the use of epithets, etc., for rhetorical effect; diffuse narrative or description, or a dilating upon all the particulars of a subject. Exaggeration is a species of amplification. Brande & C.
